title: How many bigger vehicles carry the same children on the trip?
description: The same school trip, now with tempo travellers, boats, minibuses and aeroplanes. The video divides the total by bigger numbers using tens and counting on.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide by ten, twenty, twenty five and one hundred and eighty using tens, halving and counting in jumps. Watch for children who take off one zero to divide by twenty.

video_script.why: The child must divide the total by larger numbers where simple halving or counting on is the best route.
video_script.substitution: Use friendly ways to divide: tens, halving a tenth, a hundred as four minibuses, and counting in jumps.
video_script.anchor: Joseph's school trip, the same children waiting at the gate in Kochi
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu takes off one zero to divide by twenty. Taking off one zero divides by ten only, so ninety boats would be too many.
video_script.payoff_line: thirty six minibuses and five aeroplanes

final_answer.spoken: ninety tempo travellers, forty five boats, thirty six minibuses, five aeroplanes

never_show: the total 900 shown before the hint
maths_rules: (g) 900 ÷ 25: 4 minibuses carry 4 × 25 = 100; 900 is 9 hundreds, so 9 × 4 = 36 minibuses
slip: taking off one zero gives 90, but that divides by 10, not 20
video_script.design: One idea: pick a friendly way to divide each number: tens, halving, hundreds, jumps. Wrong idea: one zero off for every divisor. The vehicle cards stay in the anchor band.

narration: <bookmark mark='m32'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m33'/>Joseph's school in Kochi has four hundred and sixty one girls and four hundred and thirty nine boys.
<bookmark mark='m34'/>The trip is the same, but the vehicles are bigger.
<bookmark mark='m35'/>Tempo travellers carry ten, and boats carry twenty.
<bookmark mark='m36'/>Minibuses carry twenty five, and aeroplanes carry one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='m37'/>How many of each are needed?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.m38: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='m38'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a hint card in the working band: find the total first; then use tens, halves or jumps to divide

marks.m39: the words find the total light up
marks.m40: the words tens, halves, jumps light up

narration: <bookmark mark='m39'/>Find the total number of children first.
<bookmark mark='m40'/>Then divide it by what one vehicle carries, using tens, halves or equal jumps.
<bookmark mark='m41'/>Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows 900 ÷ 20, take off one zero, 90; the zero in 900 is circled; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.m42: Chintu's bubble appears with 900 ÷ 20, take off one zero, 90
marks.m43: the circled zero and the words divides by ten appear
marks.m44: the number 20 splits into two tens
marks.m45: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m42'/>To divide by twenty, I take off one zero, so nine hundred becomes ninety.
<bookmark mark='m43'/>Taking off one zero divides by ten only.
<bookmark mark='m44'/>Twenty is two tens, so ninety is still too many boats.
<bookmark mark='m45'/>We must divide by two more.

beats.on_screen: the total is set out again: 461 + 439 = 900; the line 900 children in all glows
narration: <bookmark mark='m46'/>The children are the same, so the total is nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='m47'/>Four hundred and sixty one and four hundred and thirty nine make nine hundred.

beats.on_screen: two lines appear: 900 ÷ 10 = 90 tempo travellers; 900 ÷ 20: 90 ÷ 2 = 45 boats

marks.m48: the line 900 ÷ 10 = 90 appears with the tempo travellers
marks.m50: the line 90 ÷ 2 = 45 appears beside the boats

narration: <bookmark mark='m48'/>For tempo travellers, take off one zero, because the groups are ten.
<bookmark mark='m49'/>Ninety tempo travellers carry everyone.
<bookmark mark='m50'/>Twenty is two tens. Halve ninety to get forty five boats.
<bookmark mark='m51'/>Check: forty five boats of twenty make nine hundred.

beats.on_screen: two lines appear: 4 minibuses carry 100, so 9 hundreds need 36; 180 counted five times reaches 900; the four answers glow

marks.m54: a number line from 0 to 900 appears with jumps of 180
marks.m55: the first three jumps land on 180, 360, 540
marks.m56: the last two jumps land on 720 and 900

narration: <bookmark mark='m52'/>Four minibuses of twenty five carry one hundred children.
<bookmark mark='m53'/>Nine hundred is nine hundreds, so we need nine times four minibuses, which is thirty six.
<bookmark mark='m54'/>For aeroplanes, count in jumps of one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='m55'/>One hundred and eighty, then three hundred and sixty, then five hundred and forty.
<bookmark mark='m56'/>Next comes seven hundred and twenty, and then nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='m57'/>That is five aeroplanes.
<bookmark mark='m58'/>We need ninety tempo travellers and forty five boats.
<bookmark mark='m59'/>We need thirty six minibuses and five aeroplanes.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the four answers; a check line appears: vehicles multiplied by riders gives 900

marks.m60: the check line vehicles multiplied by riders appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m60'/>To check, multiply the number of vehicles by how many each one carries.
<bookmark mark='m61'/>Thirty six minibuses of twenty five make nine hundred, because four minibuses make one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m62'/>Every answer should bring you back to nine hundred.
